items.issue: The embedded video and hosts accuse identifiable people and a named business of staging encounters, hiring actors and fabricating testimonials.
items.disposition: Attribute precisely, keep unverified and exclude from factual answers without authenticated primary evidence and responses.

items.issue: The fraud-law and sentencing discussion assumes disputed facts and legal elements.
items.disposition: Require jurisdiction-specific counsel, authenticated facts and official case status; do not repeat the legal conclusion.

items.issue: Pauses, cuts, repeated angles and unnatural delivery are treated as proof of staging despite reliance on edited reaction footage.
items.disposition: Treat only as editing clues; inspect original continuous media and production records before drawing a factual conclusion.

items.issue: The episode uses facial resemblance, masked clips and editorial arrows to identify alleged students or mentors.
items.disposition: Do not identify or merge individuals without direct source verification.

items.issue: Private chats, contact lists and non-public relationship material appear in accusation and testimonial sequences.
items.disposition: Keep restricted, do not reproduce identifiers, and verify authorization before any broader use.

items.issue: Explicit sexual prompts are presented as a general route to reducing shame without consent or context safeguards.
items.disposition: Do not provide the prompts as action advice; require mutual comfort, age appropriateness and easy refusal.

items.issue: Watching neighbors through windows with a telescope or military binoculars is described as an entertaining dating activity.
items.disposition: Keep do_not_generalize; do not normalize or reproduce. Any later use must center privacy, consent and applicable law.

items.issue: The guest's very high sexual-frequency claims are unverified status claims and may encourage unsafe comparison or overexertion.
items.disposition: Do not use as a benchmark, testimonial or evidence of expertise.

items.issue: A fast-acting erectile drug is characterized as healthy and legal without product identification, ingredients, contraindications or clinician review.
items.disposition: Exclude from recommendations; require product-specific medical and regulatory verification.

items.issue: The answer to a woman's refusal after drug use substitutes another sexual act instead of stopping and respecting the refusal.
items.disposition: Do not use. State that every sexual act requires affirmative consent and medication does not create entitlement.

items.issue: The guest promotes his own service after presenting unverified sexual and industry-insider status claims.
items.disposition: Treat the surrounding claims as promotional and do not infer effectiveness.

items.issue: The limited useful principle about responding to context is mixed with allegations, conquest framing and unsafe conduct.
items.disposition: If independently reviewed, separate the context-sensitive conversation principle from all allegation and sexual-status material.

items.issue: ASR cannot reliably distinguish all embedded voices, names, drug terms and legal phrases.
items.disposition: Verify original audio and primary source material before exact quotation or speaker attribution beyond the mapped hosts.
